Array Merge Behavior (Default)

Array Merge is the default Merge behavior used by a FeatureCell when no custom merge strategy is provided. It defines how array-based state values are combined with newly resolved pipeline values during the Merge stage.

This behavior treats arrays as atomic, immutable values. When an incoming value is an array, it replaces the existing array entirely, producing a new array instance. Element-level merging, diffing, or reconciliation is intentionally not performed.

Array Merge runs within the core Merge stage and produces the merged candidate state passed to downstream pipeline stages. It does not mutate existing state, does not emit snapshots directly, and does not influence pipeline control flow beyond producing the merged value.

Note

The Merge stage is entered exclusively through explicit state-update APIs. Pipeline executions that invoke merge semantics are initiated via the mergeState method, which supply the incoming value and optional merge configuration used by the active Merge behavior.

Diagrams
Configuration

Array merge behaviors are configured as part of the Merge stage and define how array-based FeatureCell state values are combined with incoming resolved values.

Exactly one merge behavior is active for a FeatureCell at any time. If no custom array merge behavior is provided, the default withArrayMergeBehavior is applied automatically.

Merge behaviors may optionally be influenced by the clearUndefined configuration flag. When clearUndefined is enabled, an incoming undefined value is treated as an intentional clear request and results in the FeatureCell state being cleared. When disabled, incoming undefined values preserve the existing state and produce no merge output.

The clearUndefined option is supplied at the time a merge-style update is initiated and is evaluated by the active merge behavior during the Merge stage. It does not affect resolution, operators, or downstream pipeline stages.

Alternative array merge strategies may be selected to support append-style or push-style semantics. These behaviors remain purely structural and do not perform element-level reconciliation or mutation.

Evaluation Outcomes

The Array Merge behavior evaluates the current committed FeatureCell state and the incoming resolved value to produce a single merged result during the Merge stage.

Array merge treats arrays as atomic values. The incoming array replaces the existing array rather than merging individual elements. The merge result becomes the authoritative candidate state passed to downstream pipeline stages.

When the incoming value is undefined, merge behavior is controlled by the clearUndefined configuration option. This determines whether the existing state is preserved or intentionally cleared.

Example 1: Array Replacement
Inputs Merged Result
current: [1, 2, 3]

next: [9, 9]

 [9, 9] — incoming array replaces the existing array
Example 2: Undefined Incoming Value (Preserve)
Inputs Merged Result
current: [1, 2, 3]

next: undefined

clearUndefined: false

 [1, 2, 3] — existing state is preserved
Example 3: Undefined Incoming Value (Clear)
Inputs Merged Result
current: [1, 2, 3]

next: undefined

clearUndefined: true

 undefined — state is intentionally cleared
Examples

Example 1: Use the withArrayMergeBehavior in a FeatureCell

This example demonstrates a FeatureCell using the default withArrayMergeBehavior without explicitly registering a merge strategy. Incoming state updates provided via mergeState replace the existing array state entirely, producing a new immutable array instance. Because Array Merge is the default behavior, no additional configuration is required to enable this merge semantics—the FeatureCell automatically applies array replacement during the Merge stage for each merge-style update.

Note
“The withArrayMergeBehavior is the default Merge behavior and does not need to be explicitly attached to a FeatureCell.” 
{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService,
      {
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: [] 
      },
      [
        // The withArrayMergeBehavior is the default Merge behavior
        // and does not need to be attached to a FeatureCell.
      ]
    )
  ]
};
          
// bank-employee.service.ts
// The provideFeatureCell key must match the @FeatureCell key input
          
import { Injectable } from '@angular/core';
import { FeatureCell, injectVault } from '@sdux-vault/angular';
import { Employee } from './employee.shape';

@FeatureCell<Employee[]>('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {

  // Use injectVault to get an instance of the FeatureCell
  readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    // Required to activate the FeatureCell
    this.vault.initialize();
  }

  addEmployee(): void {
    this.vault.mergeState(
      {
        value: [
          { id: 1, name: 'Jane Doe' }
        ]
      }
    )
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    // The withArrayMergeBehavior is the default Merge behavior
    // and does not need to be attached to a FeatureCell.
  ],
);

// Initialization the FeatureCell 
employeeCell.initialize();

employeeCell.mergeState(
  {
    value: [
      { id: 1, name: 'Jane Doe' }
    ]
  }
)`}}
